decision: Use value-first primary labels with technical disclosure second.
rationale: Non-technical operators need to understand the business/user consequence before learning DontPanic internals. Technical IDs, source paths, and exact commands remain visible so agents, auditors, and technical operators retain precision.

decision: Treat this as a focused IA/content/design integration plan, not a new dashboard capability roadmap.
rationale: The platform already shipped operator console and project selector substrate. This plan cleans the first-read experience and integrates design assets without adding Architecture, Review, Configuration, session registry, local executor, or streaming surfaces.

decision: Keep the existing four-band status taxonomy and render optional as an orthogonal relevance chip.
rationale: Optional describes whether a capability or setup item applies to the selected profile/project. It is not a health state. Adding it as a fifth status band would reintroduce inconsistent dashboard color language.

decision: Use V0 navigation labels: Needs Attention, Work, Tools & Setup, Health, Preferences.
rationale: These labels map to what an operator or business reviewer needs to know, while still backing onto the existing What Now, Mission Control, Capability Center, status/readiness, and Settings pages.

decision: Remove or hide demo/non-core surfaces from the V0 core nav.
rationale: Financial and Cloud Costs make the product look like a Jarvis-era personal dashboard rather than DontPanic's AI-work safety console. Adapter-specific views should appear only when capability-backed and scoped, not as core tabs.
The dashboard may show exact commands and copy controls, but it must not silently mutate DontPanic state. Governed local executor and inline actions are separate future plans.

decision: Integrate Claude Design assets by adapting the existing static dashboard, not by replacing the runtime.
rationale: The current dashboard already has state projection, project selection, and What Now wiring. The design pass should improve IA, copy, components, and CSS without a framework rewrite or data substrate replacement.

decision: Explicitly add non-technical reviewer, founder, and product-owner comprehension as a V0 design audience alongside the operator-in-loop.
rationale: OSS and product review surfaces expose DontPanic to people who need business value first: what is blocked, what needs approval, what tools need setup, and whether the system is safe. This is an audience expansion, but the dashboard remains an operator console; technical substrate remains visible second.

decision: Planning-intelligence v0 is a dependency for recommended commands and lifecycle readiness language.
rationale: The Home recommended-command panel and Work readiness/stage language should use shipped `dontpanic next` substrate rather than placeholder data. Plan 2026-05-23-007 is completed and provides the read-only recommender needed for this dashboard copy/design pass.

decision: Allow drag-to-command only as a command-preview pattern; forbid drag-to-mutate in this plan.
rationale: The Claude Design work introduced drag affordances for Work. This is compatible with the read-only invariant only if dropping never changes state and instead previews or emits an exact command. If that constraint cannot be implemented cleanly, drag affordances must be removed.

decision: Use Home as an acceptable route label, but the first-viewport content must say Needs Attention; rename primary Capabilities nav to Tools & Setup or Connections.
rationale: Home is conventional and approachable for non-technical users. Capabilities is an internal platform noun and should not be the primary nav label for the setup/integrations surface.

decision: Port Claude Design output into vanilla dashboard code rather than adopting React/JSX runtime components.
rationale: Claude Design assets may arrive as JSX, but the shipped dashboard is static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Tokens and small components should be ported; full page components are visual specs. A framework rewrite is out of scope.

decision: Require fleet-mode variants for Home, Work, and Health.
rationale: The project selector substrate already shipped. A design that only works for one selected project would lose the multi-repo value DontPanic now supports. Fleet mode should group actions and warnings by project while preserving global vs project scope labels.

decision: Defer Architecture implementation to a separate interactive Architecture Explorer plan while allowing a muted future nav affordance.
rationale: The requested Roundtable-style architecture tab is a substantial graph/explorer surface, not an IA cleanup detail. This plan may signal the future surface but must not implement it.

decision: Adopt Dashboard Platform Roadmap v1 as this plan's live parent and sequence IA before Architecture shell integration.
rationale: The previous Visual Operating Console roadmap is closed. The IA plan now owns the clean V1 dashboard shell, branding, navigation, and value-language baseline. Architecture Explorer F001 may proceed in parallel as isolated substrate work, but Architecture shell/page integration should happen after this plan's nav cleanup lands or explicitly reconcile against it.

decision: Use Claude Design v3 via the dashboard-value-language IA manifest.
rationale: The operator provided DontPanic-3.zip after F001 dispatch began. The design pack is stored once under docs/design/dashboard-platform-roadmap-v1/claude-design-v3/; this plan consumes shell, token, Home, Work, Tools & Setup, Health, Preferences, empty-state, and fleet assets through docs/design/dashboard-value-language-ia-v0/claude-design-v3-manifest.md.

decision: Plan CLOSED (completed) — all 5 features operator-verified; status flipped active->completed.

Architecture surface deferred to the separate Architecture Explorer plan (D014, since shipped as 2026-05-24-002). Parent: Dashboard Platform Roadmap v1 (D015).
